capabilities: Render fenced drums code blocks as percussion staff notation
Play back notation with metronome, count-in, looping, muting, and adjustable speed
Author notation as text or edit bars visually in a grid editor
Track practice sessions with tempo ramps and repetition goals and save summaries to a practice log
Embed grooves from a library note into setlists, lesson notes, and dashboards
disambiguation: Not general music notation software; it renders and plays only drum-kit percussion staves.
extras: Also offers a browser-based web playground for trying and editing notation without installing. The plugin makes no network requests and keeps all data in the vault. The importer is versioned and released separately from the Obsidian plugin. Known limits: importer does not transcribe audio or handwritten notation; visual editing is reading-view only in v1.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to write, hear, or practise drum notation inside notes, so drummers must keep charts in separate notation software.

relations.evidence: The separately installed Drum Notation Importer Agent Plugin can transcribe a clean printed drum-score image
Production builds include VexFlow 5.0.0 for music engraving, also under the MIT License.

requires.name: ChatGPT desktop, Codex, Claude Code, or Gemini CLI

summary: Renders fenced drums code blocks as percussion staff notation with audio playback, looping, tempo-ramp practice, and visual grid editing.
